groups.title: Granules (293300AGN)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation, and for the relief of loss of appetite (reduced appetite), abdominal (belly) bloating, abnormal fermentation in the bowel and haemorrhoids that accompany constipation.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 15 years and over: take 4 g to 8 g at a time, 1 time in 1 day (in the evening) or 2 times a day (morning and evening). Do not chew it; usually take it with cold water in the morning and with warm water in the evening. Do not take this medicine just before going to bed or while lying down.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine, an acute abdominal disease (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and the like), intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel), or a stricture (narrowing) within the gastrointestinal tract.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting, if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or if you are breast-feeding.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
If constipation does not improve after several doses, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take this medicine together with cardiac glycosides.

If abdominal pain, diarrhoea or vomiting occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Constipation, and the loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, abnormal intestinal fermentation and haemorrhoids that accompany it

groups.title: Cream (345300CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for wounds at risk of infection (grazes, cuts, lacerations, burns, dermatitis), leg ulcers, pressure sores, secondarily infected eczema, skin infections such as lichen simplex chronicus (neurodermatitis), cracked (fissured) nipples during breast-feeding, and bacterial skin infection in minor surgery (skin injury, surgical wounds).
groups.usage: After cleaning the wound or the infected area of skin, apply a thin layer several times in 1 day as needed. After application the area may be treated either with or without a dressing.
groups.caution:
Direct use on the brain, the spinal cord, the ear or other auditory or central nervous tissue may cause hearing loss (deafness) and nerve disorders.

Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine or have had it, or if you have a perforated (ruptured) eardrum. Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have had an allergic condition such as asthma, if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, and especially if it is to be used around the vulva shortly before delivery. Do not use it on irritated skin that is not at particular risk of infection (for example sunburn), on mucosal surfaces such as the vagina, the bladder or the inside of the mouth, or in the eyes. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is used for a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Do not use it together with other disinfectants or preservatives. Do not combine it with surfactants or other anionic medicines.

If a burning sensation or an allergic skin reaction rarely occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Skin infections and wounds at risk of infection, including infected eczema, leg ulcers, pressure sores and cracked nipples

groups.title: Eye drops (561003COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply nutrition in ulcerative disease of the cornea and conjunctiva caused by lack of nutrition, and for fine damage to the cornea and conjunctiva caused by wearing contact lenses and the like.
groups.usage: Instil 2 to 3 drops into the eye at a time, 2 to 4 times in 1 day. After instillation, discard any solution that is left together with the container.
groups.caution:
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
When it is used for a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
Use this medicine for instillation into the eye only.
Use it only once after it has been opened.
To prevent contamination, avoid sharing it with other people as far as possible.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 2 weeks of use, stop using it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

If a hypersensitivity reaction occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Nutritional support in ulcerative disease of the cornea and conjunctiva, and fine damage from contact lens wear

groups.title: Ointment (197632COM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for impetigo (pustular crust disease), folliculitis, boils, infected eczema, and bacterial skin infection in trauma and burns, caused by most of the organisms responsible for skin infection — including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, other staphylococci and streptococci — and by Gram-negative organisms such as Escherichia coli and Haemophilus influenzae.
groups.usage: Apply a small amount to the infected area 2 to 3 times in 1 day for 10 days. If necessary the treated area may be dressed or covered with an occlusive dressing.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine or to other ointments containing polyethylene glycol, or have had such hypersensitivity, if you have kidney disease, or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding. Do not use it for a long period on exposed lacerated wounds or on damaged skin. Be careful that it does not get into the eyes. Use this medicine externally only. Do not use it on mucosal surfaces such as the eyes or the nose. Do not use it at a site where a central venous catheter is to be inserted.

If a burning sensation, stinging or aching pain, itching, rash, erythema (red patches) or another skin hypersensitivity reaction occurs, or occasionally nausea, dry skin, tenderness (pain on pressure), oedema (swelling), contact dermatitis or increased exudate, or rarely a generalised allergic reaction, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Bacterial skin infections such as impetigo, folliculitis, boils and infected eczema, and infection in wounds and burns

groups.title: Suspension (101403ASS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for fever and pain caused by a cold, headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, menstrual pain, the pain of a sprain, toothache, joint pain and rheumatic pain.
groups.usage: Children aged 12 years and under: take the recommended dose for the age at a time, every 4 to 6 hours as required. Take this medicine at the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible period, and do not take it more than 5 times in 1 day (75 mg/kg). For the recommended dose for each age group, refer to the approved product information.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine, peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder, severely reduced heart function, or aspirin asthma (an asthma attack brought on by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicines) or have had it, or if you are taking barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have liver disorder, kidney disorder, a history of peptic ulcer, a blood disorder, a tendency to bleed, abnormal heart function or a history of hypersensitivity, if you have bronchial asthma, if you are an older person, if the user is a child under 2 years of age, or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, other anti-inflammatory analgesics, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with warfarin, lithium or thiazide diuretics.

If shock symptoms (difficulty breathing, reddening of the whole body, swelling of the blood vessels, hives and the like), an asthma attack, a fall in platelets, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia, methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer, perforation, hypersensitivity symptoms (facial swelling, sweating, low blood pressure), rash, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), a rise in AST, a rise in ALT or a fixed drug eruption occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Fever and pain from a cold, headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, menstrual pain, sprain pain, toothache, joint pain and rheumatic pain

groups.title: Vaginal tablet (338800CTB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for bacterial vaginosis.
groups.usage: Adults: insert 1 tablet deep into the vagina at a time, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.
Use this medicine in the vagina only; it is not for internal use as a medicine that is swallowed.
This medicine can weaken latex and rubber products such as condoms and vaginal diaphragms, so please be careful.

If a feeling of irritation or a similar reaction occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Eye drops (D49002COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for dryness of the eye (discomfort, stinging pain, irritation) and for tired eyes caused by wind, smoke, pollution, dust, dry heat, air conditioning, air travel or long periods of computer use.
groups.usage: Instil 1 drop into each eye at a time, several times in 1 day as required. After instillation, discard any solution that is left together with the container. For a preservative-free multi-dose product only, use it for up to 4 weeks after it has been opened.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine or to protein-based medicines.
Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have severe eye pain, if you have ever had an allergic reaction to an eye medicine (for example redness of the eye, itching, swelling, rash or reddening), or if you have glaucoma.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
Use this medicine for instillation into the eye only.
Wash your hands thoroughly before use.
If the tip of the container touches the eyelid or the eyelashes, the solution may become contaminated or cloudy from eye discharge or mould, so be careful not to let it touch the eye directly. Also, do not use the solution if it has become cloudy.
Do not share it with other people, to prevent contamination.
This medicine may be used while contact lenses are being worn.
If symptoms get worse, or last for 3 days or more, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

If it is used at the same time as another eye drop, use the other eye drop first and instil this medicine about 10 minutes later.

If eye irritation rarely occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Cream (A24400CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of pain and inflammation in varicose swelling, superficial phlebitis, injury from an accident, sports injury (bruising) and tenosynovitis.
groups.usage: Apply a thin layer to the injured or affected area several times in 1 day, then rub the skin gently.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine or to salicylates, if you are within 4 weeks of your delivery date, or on mucosal areas or open wounds. Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a newborn or a child, if you have kidney failure, or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Be careful not to let it get into the eyes, and do not apply it over too wide an area. Use it externally only. When it is used for a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Bleeding may increase when it is used together with other anticoagulants (for example coumarin, aspirin, dipyridamole, dextran or streptokinase), so consult a doctor or pharmacist.

If dermatitis, contact allergy, tinnitus (ringing in the ears) with hearing impairment, nosebleed, nausea, vomiting, itching, or dryness of the skin and mucous membranes rarely occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Powder (448301APD)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation.
groups.usage: Adults: dissolve 17 g in about 240 mL of water, juice, soda, coffee or tea and take it in the morning where possible, 1 time in 1 day. It takes about 1 to 4 days (24 to 96 hours) for a bowel movement to be produced.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine, inflammatory bowel disease (ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease and the like), toxic megacolon, intestinal perforation or a risk of intestinal perforation, intestinal obstruction or suspected intestinal obstruction, intestinal stricture, or abdominal pain of unknown cause. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, if the user is a child or an adolescent, if you have kidney disease or irritable bowel syndrome, if a sudden change in bowel habit has lasted for 2 weeks or more, if you are on a sodium-restricted diet, or if you are on a low-potassium diet. If constipation does not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

When you are taking other medicines, do not take them together with this medicine within 2 hours.

If nausea, abdominal bloating, cramping, abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, involuntary passing of stool, upper abdominal pain, stomach irritation or rectal bleeding, an anaphylactic reaction, an allergic reaction such as hives, rash, itching or swelling, or occasionally headache or dizziness occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Constipation

groups.title: Tablet (244302ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for disturbance of digestive function (abdominal pain, indigestion, nausea, vomiting) in oesophageal reflux and hiatus hernia, in gastritis and duodenitis and in gastric and duodenal ulcer; for irritable bowel syndrome and spastic colon; and for disorders in children (non-infectious disturbance of intestinal transit such as habitual vomiting, constipation and diarrhoea).
groups.usage: Adults: take 0.5 to 1 tablet (100 to 200 mg) at a time, 3 times in 1 day, before meals. The dose may be increased or decreased as appropriate according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to Food Yellow No. 4 or have had it, or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Rarely, constipation, diarrhoea, rumbling in the bowel, nausea, vomiting, digestive disturbance, thirst, a feeling of numbness in the mouth, palpitations, tiredness, drowsiness, dizziness, a feeling of malaise, headache, or a rise in GOT and GPT may occur. If a rash or a similar reaction rarely occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Digestive disturbance in reflux, gastritis and duodenitis and peptic ulcer; irritable bowel syndrome and spastic colon; childhood transit disorders

groups.title: Chewing gum (A88102AMS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as an aid to giving up smoking: it reduces the amount smoked and helps you to stop smoking.
groups.usage: For smokers who smoke 20 cigarettes or fewer a day the 2 mg gum is recommended; for heavy smokers who smoke more than 20 cigarettes a day, or for those in whom the 2 mg strength has not worked, the 4 mg gum is recommended. Follow the steps below, chewing the gum for 30 minutes and then discarding the used gum. Put 1 piece of the gum in the mouth and chew it slowly, with a few seconds between chews. Chew until a strong taste or a slight tingling is felt, then rest the gum inside the cheek until the strong taste or tingling settles. Then chew slowly again and repeat as above. Continue in this way for 30 minutes. Once you are used to the taste of the gum, increase the chewing rate as needed. To stay completely free of smoking, use the gum whenever there is an urge to smoke. Usually chew 8 to 12 pieces of the 2 mg or the 4 mg gum a day, and do not let the total daily use go above 15 pieces. As the urge to smoke gradually falls, reduce the number of pieces used in 1 day. It is generally used for about 3 months.
groups.caution:
It may stick to dental prostheses and dentures and, in rare cases, may damage them.

Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, unstable angina, worsening angina, a myocardial infarction within the last 3 months, the late period after an acute infarction, a severe cardiac arrhythmia, generalised high blood pressure, peripheral vascular disease, an acute stroke or cerebrovascular disease; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a child or adolescent under 18 years of age; if you are a non-smoker or an occasional smoker; or if you have hereditary fructose intolerance. Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have gastritis, gastric or duodenal ulcer, occlusive arterial disease, stable angina, heart failure, decompensated heart failure, myocardial infarction, cardiac arrhythmia, vasospasm, uncontrolled high blood pressure, an arterial bypass graft or angioplasty, if you are an older person, or if you have kidney failure, liver failure, diabetes, an overactive thyroid or a phaeochromocytoma, or if you are a smoker who wears dentures. Dental fillings or implants may become loose.

Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you use it together with paracetamol, caffeine, imipramine, oxazepam, pentazocine, propranolol, theophylline, warfarin, oestrogens, lignocaine, phenacetin, insulin, adrenergic antagonists (prazosin, labetalol and the like), flecainide, adrenergic agonists (isoprenaline, phenylephrine), propoxyphene, furosemide diuretics, H2 antagonists, beta blockers, tacrine, clozapine or ropinirole.

If headache, dizziness, sleep disturbance, anxiety, emotional instability, agitation, abnormal dreams, confusion, restlessness, difficulty concentrating, tiredness, migraine, spasm (contraction and relaxation), leg cramps, changes in blood pressure, high blood pressure, palpitations, reversible atrial fibrillation, atrial arrhythmia, nausea, vomiting, upper abdominal pain, abdominal pain, indigestion, flatulence (abdominal bloating), a gastrointestinal disorder such as gastric ulcer, difficulty swallowing, thirst, altered bowel habit, constipation, diarrhoea, increased appetite, cold or influenza symptoms, cough, pharyngitis, rhinitis, sinusitis, upper respiratory symptoms, bronchitis, difficulty breathing, allergy, skin rash, herpes eruption, itching, hives, acne, erythema (red patches), altered taste, abnormal vision, irritation (pain) of the mouth and throat, pain in the jaw joint and muscles, gingivitis, painful menstruation, muscle pain, joint pain, toothache, back pain, chest pain, pain, earache, facial flushing, local oedema (swelling), weight gain, thyroid dysfunction, painful lymph nodes, cystitis, increased sweating, hiccups or angioedema (swelling) occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft capsule (347904ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of nasal allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose and blocked nose caused by pollen, house dust or indoor dust.
groups.usage: Adults and adolescents aged 15 years and over: take 1 capsule at a time, 2 times in 1 day, in the morning and in the evening.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have had hypersensitivity to it, or if the user is a child under 15 years of age.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you do not know whether the symptoms are due to allergic rhinitis or to another cause such as a cold, if you have been diagnosed with another allergic condition, if the blocked nose is severe, if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, if you are breast-feeding, if you are an older person, if you have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine, if you have kidney disorder, or if you have cardiovascular disease.
Avoid breast-feeding while you are taking this medicine.
Do not go above the recommended dose.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take medicines for skin conditions, other allergy medicines including oral medicines for rhinitis, other oral medicines containing antihistamines, or antacids containing aluminium or magnesium.
While you are taking this medicine, do not take it together with ketoconazole or erythromycin.
While you are taking this medicine, do not take it with fruit juices or foods such as grapefruit juice, orange juice or apple juice.
Do not drink alcohol before or after a dose.

If dry mouth, constipation, diarrhoea, drowsiness, swelling of the throat, eyelids or lips, rash, itching, hives, reddening of the skin, queasiness, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, numbness, headache, tiredness, malaise, dizziness, insomnia, nervousness, nightmares, sleep disturbance, frequent urination, difficulty passing urine, palpitations, altered taste, oedema (swelling), chest pain, difficulty breathing, a rise in blood pressure or menstrual disturbance occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Rarely, shock (anaphylaxis) — with itching of the skin, hives, a hoarse voice, sneezing, itching of the throat, difficulty breathing, palpitations or clouding of consciousness appearing immediately after a dose — or agranulocytosis, a fall in white cells or neutropenia — with fever, jaundice, brown urine, generalised weakness, loss of appetite, sudden high fever, chills or sore throat — may occur; if so, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Granules (101843AGN)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for difficulty in bringing up sputum in acute and chronic bronchitis, bronchial asthma, laryngitis, sinusitis and cystic fibrosis.
groups.usage: For acute disease: adults take 1 sachet (200 mg) at a time, 3 times in 1 day; those aged 6 to 14 years take 1 sachet (200 mg) at a time, 2 times in 1 day; and those aged 2 to 5 years take 1/2 sachet (100 mg) at a time, 3 times in 1 day, each with a small amount of water. For chronic disease: adults take 1 sachet (200 mg) at a time, 2 times in 1 day, and those aged 6 to 14 years take 1/2 sachet (100 mg) at a time, 3 times in 1 day, each with a small amount of water. For cystic fibrosis: those aged 6 years and over take 1 sachet (200 mg) at a time, 3 times in 1 day, and those aged 2 to 5 years take 1/2 sachet (100 mg) at a time, 4 times in 1 day, each with a small amount of water.
groups.caution:
This medicine contains aspartame, which is broken down in the body to phenylalanine, so people with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their intake of phenylalanine must not take it.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, gastric or duodenal ulcer, or if the user is an infant under 2 years of age. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

When it is taken with oral antibiotics (amoxicillin, cefuroxime, doxycycline, erythromycin, thiamphenicol), leave an interval of at least 2 hours between them. Avoid adding other medicines to the solution of this medicine.

If nausea, vomiting, stomatitis, heartburn, diarrhoea, hives, itching, rash, headache, tinnitus, bronchospasm (especially in people with asthma), rapid heartbeat or high blood pressure rarely occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Difficulty bringing up sputum in acute and chronic bronchitis, bronchial asthma, laryngitis, sinusitis and cystic fibrosis

groups.title: Paste (243335CPA)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of inflammation due to chronic desquamative gingivitis and to intractable stomatitis and glossitis accompanied by erosion or ulceration.
groups.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area 1 to several times in 1 day. The amount may be increased or decreased as appropriate according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, a tuberculous, viral or other pus-forming infection of the mouth, syphilis, chickenpox, a fungal infection, a bacterial skin infection, dermatitis around the mouth, rosacea, or gingivitis due to lack of vitamin C. Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to propylene glycol or have had it, if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, if the user is an infant or a child, or if the user is an older person. Do not eat food immediately after use. Do not use it for the eyes.

Slight discomfort such as a feeling of numbness in the mouth, an abnormal or reduced sense of taste, or an unusual feeling at the site of use may occur. If a fungal or bacterial infection of the mouth or, rarely, an allergic skin reaction occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (185102ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for acute diarrhoea and chronic diarrhoea.
groups.usage:
Adults with acute diarrhoea: take 2 capsules (4 mg), and then, as a maintenance dose, 1 capsule (2 mg) each time a loose stool is passed. The usual daily amount is 3 to 4 capsules (6 to 8 mg) and the maximum amount in 1 day is 8 capsules (16 mg).
Adults with chronic diarrhoea: take 2 capsules (4 mg) as the first dose, and then 1 capsule (2 mg) each time a loose stool is passed until the diarrhoea is controlled. After that the dose is reduced to suit the individual person. Once the best daily dose has been decided, take it as 1 dose in 1 day or divided into 2 doses in 1 day. The usual maintenance dose is 1 to 3 capsules (2 to 6 mg) in 1 day, and the maximum amount in 1 day is 8 capsules (16 mg).
Children aged 9 to 12 years with acute diarrhoea: take 1 capsule (2 mg), and then, as a maintenance dose, 1 capsule (2 mg) each time a loose stool is passed. The maximum amount in 1 day is 3 capsules (6 mg).
The dose may be increased or decreased as appropriate according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is an infant or child under 24 months of age; if you have bacterial diarrhoea with bloody stools and high fever, acute ulcerative colitis, pseudomembranous colitis associated with broad-spectrum antibiotics, intestinal obstruction, megacolon, toxic megacolon or haemorrhagic colitis; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have liver disorder, if you have hypersensitivity to Food Yellow No. 5 or have had it, if you have diarrhoea, if you have AIDS, if you are pregnant, may become pregnant or are breast-feeding, or if you are an older person.
Loss of body fluid and electrolytes may occur, so fluid and electrolytes should be replaced appropriately.
Tiredness, dizziness or drowsiness may occur after a dose, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.
If symptoms do not improve within 48 hours in acute diarrhoea, or within 10 days in chronic diarrhoea, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Use in infants and young children aged 7 years and under is not recommended.

Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with quinidine or ritonavir.

Abdominal pain or discomfort, nausea, vomiting, thirst, tiredness, drowsiness, dizziness, constipation and flatulence may occur.

groups.title: Tablet (221603ATB)

groups.usage: Adults: take 10 mg (1/5 tablet) to 100 mg (2 tablets) in 1 day. In vitamin B6 dependency a higher dose may be taken.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you are receiving levodopa, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist, because when it is used in large amounts in newborn babies and infants rhabdomyolysis may occur and serious kidney damage such as acute kidney failure may follow. When it is given to a newborn baby or an infant, start with a small amount and increase it slowly until the amount that suits the symptoms is reached. If you are pregnant or breast-feeding, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking it. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not use it together with levodopa, altretamine or cisplatin. Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with isoniazid, penicillamine or oestrogen preparations (for example oral contraceptives), which increase the requirement for vitamin B6.

Photosensitivity, nausea, headache and drowsiness may occur. If rhabdomyolysis — shown by a rise in creatine kinase and a rise in myoglobin in the blood and the urine — acute kidney failure, diarrhoea, vomiting or abnormal liver function occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Prevention and treatment of vitamin B6 deficiency and dependency, and conditions such as cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and peripheral neuritis linked to it

groups.title: Patch (A88117CPC)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as an aid when giving up smoking.
groups.usage: Adults: apply 1 patch 1 time in 1 day to a hairless part of the body (the buttock, the inner arm and the like), changing the site of application every day. The TTS 30 patch is generally used for smokers who smoke 20 cigarettes or more a day, and the TTS 20 patch for smokers of up to 20 cigarettes a day. The TTS 10 patch is used at the final stage to reduce the nicotine replacement. Heavy smokers start with the TTS 30 patch, then move to the TTS 20 patch and finally to the TTS 10 patch, each for 4 weeks. Ordinary smokers use the TTS 20 patch for 8 weeks and then the TTS 10 patch for 4 weeks. Treatment must not go beyond 3 months.
groups.caution:
If you continue to smoke while using this medicine, cardiovascular side effects from nicotine may occur more often and more markedly, so it must be used only by people who have stopped smoking completely.

Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, a chronic skin disease (psoriasis, chronic dermatitis, hives), a generalised skin disease or hypersensitivity dermatitis, unstable angina, worsening angina, a myocardial infarction within the last 3 months, the late period after an acute infarction, a severe cardiac arrhythmia, generalised high blood pressure, peripheral vascular disease or cerebrovascular disease (acute stroke, abnormality of the blood vessels of the brain); if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; if the user is a child or adolescent under 18 years of age; or if you are a non-smoker or an occasional smoker. Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have gastritis, peptic ulcer, occlusive arterial disease, stable angina, heart failure, decompensated heart failure, myocardial infarction, cardiac arrhythmia, vasospasm, uncontrolled high blood pressure, an arterial bypass graft or angioplasty, kidney failure, liver failure, diabetes, an overactive thyroid or a phaeochromocytoma.

Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you use it together with paracetamol, caffeine, imipramine, oxazepam, pentazocine, propranolol, theophylline, warfarin, oestrogens, lignocaine, phenacetin, insulin, adrenergic antagonists (prazosin, labetalol and the like), flecainide, adrenergic agonists (isoprenaline, phenylephrine), propoxyphene, furosemide diuretics, H2 antagonists, beta blockers, tacrine, clozapine or ropinirole.

If erythema (red patches), a burning sensation, blisters, skin rash or tightness at the site of application, agitation, anxiety, nervousness, insomnia, abnormal dreams, headache, dizziness, abnormal movement, difficulty paying attention, drowsiness, emotional instability, irritability, depression, confusion, tremor, palpitations, high blood pressure, flushing, chest pain, difficulty breathing, irregular heartbeat, cough, upper respiratory infection, nausea, abdominal pain, indigestion, vomiting, constipation, diarrhoea, abdominal bloating, dry mouth, a skin reaction at the site of application, excessive sweating, loss of skin colour, vasculitis of the skin, pain or discomfort at the site of application, muscle pain, arthritis, weakness, joint pain, muscle spasm, back pain, hives, rash, itching, angioedema (swelling) or an anaphylaxis-like reaction occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (487401ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to restore and normalise the balance of bacteria in the bowel.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and over: take 1 capsule at a time, 2 times in 1 day, with a meal or within 30 minutes after a meal.
groups.caution:
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if your immunity is reduced — for example by immune deficiency, cancer chemotherapy or an organ transplant — if you have had endocarditis or myocarditis and have had surgery, if you have bloody diarrhoea, if the user is an infant with short bowel syndrome, or if you have diabetes or impaired function of the pancreas. In people with insulin-dependent diabetes, monitor the blood sugar level and adjust the insulin intake appropriately. If the contents of the capsule are taken separately, always take them with a cold drink or cold food.

If sepsis occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (385300ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for stomach pain, abdominal pain, colic, excess stomach acid and heartburn.
groups.usage: Adults aged 15 years and over: take 2 tablets at a time, 2 to 3 times in 1 day, after or before meals. When it is taken 2 or more times in 1 day, leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
Children aged 7 years and under, and people with a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption, must not take this medicine.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to medicines, heart disorder, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine, if you are physically weak or an older person, or if you are pregnant or may be pregnant.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
Blurred vision and sensitivity to light may occur after a dose, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with preparations containing scopolia extract, or with gastrointestinal analgesic and antispasmodic medicines.

If rash, itching, thirst, constipation, headache, facial flushing, sensitivity to light or difficulty passing urine occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (D21100ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 2 capsules at a time. Children over 7 years of age and under 15 years of age: take 1 capsule at a time. Take it 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.
Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported; if a skin rash or another sign of hypersensitivity appears after a dose of this medicine, stop taking it at once.
Do not go above the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had it, if you have had asthma when taking another antipyretic analgesic or cold medicine, if the user is an infant under 3 months of age or a child under 2 years of age, or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the last 2 weeks.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain, blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain or another stomach problem that lasts or comes back, or an ulcer or a bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you smoke, or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with a lot of phlegm, a cough lasting or coming back for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or a persistent headache; or if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Food Yellow No. 5.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
Drowsiness may occur after a dose, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 5 or 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take it together with cough and expectorant medicines, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, travel sickness medicines, allergy medicines).
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol.
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.

If rash or reddening, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema (swelling), difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, or rarely shock (hives, swelling and tightness of the chest immediately after a dose, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, generalised weakness, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes) or interstitial pneumonia (cough with shortness of breath, difficulty breathing and fever), stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Relief of cold symptoms — runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint and muscle pain

groups.title: Powder (164431APD)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to improve indigestion caused by primary lactose intolerance and by secondary lactose intolerance (simple diarrhoea, acute indigestion, diarrhoea with a cold, white-stool diarrhoea, chronic diarrhoea, diarrhoea in premature and newborn babies, and diarrhoea from lactose intolerance when tube feeds or oral liquid feeds are taken).
groups.usage: For indigestion due to lactose intolerance in infants: take 1,250 to 2,500 ONPG units of beta-galactosidase at a time, together with a feed. For a breast-fed infant, dissolve it in a small amount of water and take it during the feed; for a formula-fed infant, mix it into the formula. Take care that the temperature of the made-up formula does not go above 50℃. For diarrhoea due to lactose intolerance when tube feeds or oral liquid feeds are taken: take 5,000 ONPG units with the meal for every 10 g of lactose taken. The amount may be increased or decreased as appropriate according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have hives, bronchial asthma, hypersensitivity to other medicines or food allergy. If the condition of the stool does not improve and the number of bowel movements does not fall, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

If shock symptoms (cold hands and feet, pallor of the face, cyanosis, diarrhoea, abdominal bloating, vomiting and the like) occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Rash, constipation, abdominal bloating and vomiting may rarely occur.

summaryTable.What it is for: Indigestion caused by primary and secondary lactose intolerance

groups.title: Syrup (684000ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for cough and phlegm in acute and chronic respiratory disease (bronchitis, pharyngolaryngitis, nasopharyngitis and the like), and for cough in influenza and colds in children.
groups.usage: Children aged 3 years and over but under 12 years: take 5 ml at a time, usually 3 times in 1 day. Adults and those aged 12 years and over: take 10 ml at a time, usually 3 times in 1 day. The dose may be increased or decreased as appropriate according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, gastric or duodenal ulcer, or if you have had hypersensitivity to this medicine or to similar compounds; if you have glaucoma or a disease that obstructs the lower urinary tract such as an enlarged prostate; or if the user is a premature baby or a newborn.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have raised pressure inside the eye, an overactive thyroid, a narrowing peptic ulcer or obstruction of the pylorus and duodenum, disease of the circulation such as cardiovascular disease or high blood pressure, epilepsy, bronchitis, bronchiectasis or asthma, or liver disease; if the user is a newborn baby; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you are an older person.
Drowsiness may occur after a dose, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.
It may cause slight irritation to the skin, the eyes and the mucous membranes.
Avoid adding other medicines to the solution of this medicine.

When it is taken with amoxicillin, cefuroxime, doxycycline, erythromycin or thiamphenicol, leave an interval of at least 2 hours between them.
Taking it together with alcohol or medicines that depress the central nervous system may cause drowsiness.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with chlorpheniramine.

If nausea, vomiting, stomatitis, heartburn, diarrhoea, hives, itching, rash, headache, tinnitus, bronchospasm (especially in people with asthma), rapid heartbeat, high blood pressure, shock, cyanosis, difficulty breathing, chest discomfort, a fall in blood pressure, seizures, confusion, aplastic anaemia, agranulocytosis, rash, photosensitivity, exfoliative dermatitis, hives, spasm, muscle weakness, poor coordination, sedation, drowsiness, nervousness, headache, agitation, double vision, insomnia, dizziness, tinnitus, a balance disorder, euphoria, emotional instability, hysteria, tremor, neuritis, incoordination, altered sensation, inattention, reduced concentration, malaise, thirst, heartburn, loss of appetite, indigestion, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, constipation, diarrhoea, frequent urination, difficulty passing urine, retention of urine, dryness of the nose or the airway, thickening of bronchial secretions, wheezing, blocked nose, haemolytic anaemia, a fall in platelets, chills, abnormal sweating, chest pain, tiredness or menstrual disturbance rarely occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.usage: Adults: take 3/4 to 1 sachet, 1 to 3 times in 1 day, after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have an acute abdominal disease (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis) or intestinal obstruction, if you are breast-feeding, or if the user is an infant under 3 months of age. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, if the user is an infant under 1 year of age, if you have an allergic constitution, or if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea, queasiness or vomiting. If constipation does not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not use it together with other laxatives.

If rash or reddening, itching, severe abdominal pain, queasiness or vomiting, or diarrhoea occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Enteric-coated tablet (E26500ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation and for the relief of the loss of appetite (reduced appetite), abdominal bloating, abnormal fermentation in the bowel and haemorrhoid symptoms that follow constipation.
groups.usage: Those aged 15 years and over: take 1 to 2 tablets at a time, 1 time in 1 day, at bedtime (or on an empty stomach). For the first dose take the smallest amount, and then increase or decrease it little by little while watching the form and condition of the stool.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have an acute abdominal disease (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and the like), intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel), or a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, if the user is a child aged 10 years or under, if you have an allergic constitution, severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting, if you are on a sodium-restricted diet, if you have had rectal bleeding or bowel failure, or if you have hypersensitivity to Food Yellow No. 4 or have had it.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
Do not chew the tablet.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 week of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take it together with antacids.
Do not take this medicine within 1 hour after drinking milk.

If rash, reddening, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramping occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Eye drops (401637COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of dryness of the eye and for the temporary relief of irritation.
groups.usage: Instil 1 to 2 drops into the eye as required. The amount may be increased or decreased as appropriate according to symptoms. After instillation, discard any solution that is left together with the container straight away.
groups.caution:
Use it for instillation into the eye only.
When instilling it, be careful that the opening of the container does not touch the eye directly.
To prevent contamination, avoid sharing it with other people as far as possible.
Do not use the solution if its colour has changed or if it has become cloudy.
Do not use it if the safety seal on the cap is broken.

If there is pain in the eye or a change in vision, continuing redness or a feeling of irritation, or if symptoms last for 72 hours or more, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Oral liquid (D62800ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin B6 in pregnancy and breast-feeding and when strength is reduced during or after an illness, and for the relief of muscle cramps caused by magnesium deficiency and of angular cheilitis (inflammation at the corners of the mouth), cheilitis (inflammation of the lips), stomatitis (inflammation inside the mouth), glossitis (inflammation of the tongue), eczema and dermatitis.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and over: take 10 mL at a time, 2 times in 1 day, between meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a baby under 12 months of age, or if you have severe heart failure.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney disorder or a low protein level in the blood, if you are pregnant, or if you have hypersensitivity to caramel or have had it.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
This medicine is for oral use only; do not use it for injection.

Do not take it together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with anti-aldosterone medicines or triamterene.
Avoid tea containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, during the period of use and just before and after a dose.

If red patches, diarrhoea, cardiac arrest (stopping of the heartbeat) or reduced function of the central nervous system occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Cream (165138CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for primary skin infections (contagious impetigo, superficial folliculitis, ecthyma, boils, sycosis) and for secondary skin infections (infected eczema-like dermatitis, pustular psoriasis, seborrhoeic dermatitis and contact dermatitis with secondary infection by pus-forming bacteria, wounds and pustular acne, and mixed infection with a fungal or viral infection).
groups.usage: Apply to the affected area 1 to 4 times in 1 day and rub in gently. Gauze may be placed over it if needed. In contagious impetigo it is best to remove the crust first, taking care not to contaminate other normal skin, and then apply it.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to other aminoglycoside antibiotics (streptomycin, kanamycin, gentamicin, neomycin) or to bacitracin, or if the user is an infant under 1 year of age.
Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, or if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to propylene glycol.
Use it only for the shortest period needed for treatment.
Do not use it for the eyes.

If excessive growth of insensitive organisms, skin irritation (erythema, itching and the like), a hypersensitivity reaction, a superimposed infection or signs of sensitisation (reddening, swelling, papules, small blisters) occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Syrup (101342ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for fever and pain caused by a cold, headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, menstrual pain, the pain of a sprain, toothache, joint pain and rheumatic pain.
groups.usage: Children aged 12 years and under: take the recommended dose for the age at a time, every 4 to 6 hours as required. Take this medicine at the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible period, and do not take it more than 5 times in 1 day (75 mg/kg). For the dose for each age group, refer to the approved product information.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.
Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) — have been reported; if a skin rash or another sign of hypersensitivity appears after a dose of this medicine, stop taking it at once.
Do not go above the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder or severely reduced heart function; if you have aspirin asthma (an asthma attack brought on by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicines) or have had it; if you are taking barbiturates or tricyclic antidepressants; or if you have taken alcohol.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have liver disorder or have had it, kidney disorder or have had it, a history of peptic ulcer, a blood disorder or have had one, a tendency to bleed, abnormal heart function or a history of hypersensitivity, bronchial asthma, if you are an older person, if the user is a child under 2 years of age, if you are pregnant or breast-feeding, or if you have been taking warfarin over a long period.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have been taking lithium or thiazide diuretics.

If shock symptoms (difficulty breathing, reddening of the whole body, swelling of the blood vessels, hives and the like), an asthma attack, a fall in platelets, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia (destruction of red cells), methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, hypersensitivity symptoms (facial swelling, difficulty breathing, sweating, low blood pressure), nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal effects such as gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer or perforation with long-term use, rash, an allergic reaction, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), a rise in AST, a rise in ALT or a fixed drug eruption occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
If pain or fever lasts or gets worse, or if new symptoms appear, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule (200 mg) at a time, 2 times in 1 day.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, or if the user is an infant under 2 years of age.

If a generalised allergic reaction (reddening of the skin, itching, a burning sensation) or a local reaction rarely occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Enteric-coated tablet (A27400ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation and for the relief of the loss of appetite (reduced appetite), abdominal (belly) bloating, abnormal fermentation in the bowel and haemorrhoids that accompany constipation.
groups.usage: Those aged 15 years and over: take 2 tablets at a time. Those aged 11 years and over but under 15 years: take 1 1/3 tablets at a time. Those aged 8 years and over but under 11 years: take 1 tablet at a time. Take it 1 time in 1 day at bedtime. For the first dose take the smallest amount, and then increase or decrease it little by little while watching the form and condition of the stool.
groups.caution:
Children aged 7 years and under, and people with an acute abdominal disease (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and the like), intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel), or a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption, must not take this medicine. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, if the user is a child aged 10 years or under, if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting, or if you have had rectal bleeding or bowel failure. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If constipation does not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Do not chew the tablet.

Do not take it together with antacids. Avoid taking it within 1 hour after drinking milk.

If rash or reddening, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramping occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft capsule (246501ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as supportive treatment for liver disease and for disease of the biliary system (the bile ducts and the gallbladder) arising from insufficient secretion of bile, to improve liver function in chronic liver disease, and for indigestion after removal of part of the small bowel and in inflammatory disease of the small bowel.
groups.usage: Take 1/2 to 1 capsule (50 mg to 100 mg as ursodeoxycholic acid) at a time, 3 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, severe obstruction of the bile duct, fulminant hepatitis, radio-opaque calcified gallstones or a non-functioning gallbladder; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a child; if you have kidney disease, peptic ulcer (acute gastric or duodenal ulcer), or inflammation of the large or small bowel such as Crohn's disease; or if you are hypersensitive to soya, peanut or soya-bean oil or have a history of allergy to them.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or if fat emulsions must be given to you with care; if you have hypersensitivity to Food Yellow No. 5 or have had it; if you have severe disease of the pancreas; if you have gallstones in the bile duct; if you have bleeding from varices, hepatic coma or ascites (fluid in the abdomen); if you may suddenly need a liver transplant; or if fat overload would place you at particular risk.

Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with oral medicines for diabetes (tolbutamide), cholestyramine, colestipol, medicinal charcoal, antacids containing magnesium and aluminium hydroxide, medicines that increase the secretion of cholesterol from the liver (for example oral contraceptives containing oestrogen, or lipid-lowering medicines such as clofibrate), or medicines that damage the liver.

If diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting or itching occurs from time to time, or rarely abdominal pain, constipation, heartburn, stomach discomfort, rash, fever, cough, difficulty breathing, interstitial pneumonia with an abnormal chest X-ray, generalised malaise, dizziness, calcification of gallstones, a rise in liver enzymes (ALT, ALP, AST, GT) or a fall in white cells, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Eye drops (B93700COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for tired eyes, redness of the conjunctiva, prevention of eye disease (discomfort of the eye after swimming, or when dust or sweat has got into the eye), inflammation of the eye caused by ultraviolet and other light, soreness of the eyelids, discomfort when hard contact lenses are worn, itching of the eye, and blurring of the eye (for example when there is a lot of eye discharge).
groups.usage: Instil 1 to 3 drops into the eye at a time, 3 to 6 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Infants aged 30 months and under must not use this medicine.
Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have severe pain in the eye, if you have had an allergy to an eye medicine, if you have an allergic constitution, if you have glaucoma, or if the user is a child.
Use this medicine for instillation into the eye only.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
When it is used for a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
Do not use it as a wetting solution for soft contact lenses, and do not use it while soft contact lenses are being worn.
To prevent contamination, avoid sharing it with other people as far as possible.
Do not use it after the expiry date, and once it has been opened use it as soon as possible.

If redness of the eye, itching or swelling occurs, or a skin rash, or if blurring of the eye does not improve, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.usage: Adults: take 1 to 2 tablets at a time, 1 time in 1 day, at bedtime (or on an empty stomach). For the first dose take the smallest amount, and then increase or decrease it little by little while watching the form and condition of the stool.

groups.title: Cream (658500CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the early treatment of recurrent cold sores of the lip (herpes labialis).
groups.usage: Adults: use an amount large enough to cover the affected area right up to its edge, 5 times in 1 day, for 5 days. Limit the treatment period with this medicine to 5 days or less. Start treatment as soon as possible, as soon as the first symptoms and signs appear.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have a skin infection (tuberculosis, syphilis, candidiasis, ringworm, shingles, chickenpox, vaccinia, scabies, pubic lice); if your immune system is damaged (bone-marrow transplant or AIDS); if you have eczematous otitis externa with a perforated eardrum, an ulcer (except in Behçet's disease), a deep second-degree or worse burn or frostbite, dermatitis around the mouth, common acne or rosacea; if you are breast-feeding; if the user is under 18 years of age; or if you have or have had a myocardial infarction.
Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or if you are an older person.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
Use it only for cold sores on the lips or around the mouth; do not use it in the eyes, the nose, the mouth or on the genitals.
Do not use it in people who have no signs or symptoms.
Do not use it to prevent infection of other people or to prevent recurrent herpes simplex infection.
Do not use this medicine as a base for diluting or mixing other medicines.

Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you use it together with probenecid.

Dryness and peeling of the skin occur commonly, and a temporary burning sensation or numbness occurs from time to time. If erythema, pigmentation, a reaction at the site of application including signs and symptoms of inflammation, contact dermatitis, contagious impetigo, folliculitis, candidiasis, ringworm, a boil, skin irritation, stinging pain, fever, a burning sensation, rash, reddening, flushing, itching, dry skin, pustular dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, prickly heat, sweat rash, worsening of a wound, a pressure sore or pustules occurs, or if raised pressure inside the eye or glaucoma (blurred vision, impaired sight) occurs when it is used on the skin of the eyelid, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Absorption into the body may cause reversible Cushing's syndrome, a high blood sugar level, sugar in the urine and visual disturbance.

groups.title: Oral liquid (158632ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for iron deficiency anaemia.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 bottle (100 mg as iron), 1 time in 1 day. Children aged 12 years and over but under 19 years: take 1/2 bottle (50 mg as iron) at a time, 2 times in 1 day. Children aged 1 year and over but under 12 years: take 1/2 bottle (50 mg as iron) at a time, 1 to 2 times in 1 day. Take it before a meal, during a meal or after a meal.
groups.caution:
An overdose in a child aged 6 years or under can cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep it out of the reach of children.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is an infant under 12 months of age; if you have haemochromatosis (a disease in which iron is deposited in the liver and pancreas because of abnormal iron metabolism), haemosiderosis, anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency, a disorder of iron use, iron overload, anaemia due to bone-marrow failure, chronic haemolytic anaemia, iron deficiency anaemia due to infection or tumour, chronic pancreatitis or cirrhosis of the liver.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional colitis, impaired heart or circulatory function, paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria, kidney disorder, or a low protein level in the blood.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Do not take it together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics or antacids. Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with iron-containing preparations (iron supplements, liver contrast agents for MRI and the like), anti-aldosterone medicines, triamterene, diphosphonates, thyroxine, cefdinir preparations, quinolones, penicillamine, cholestyramine, pancreatic extract, preparations such as vitamin E, or 200 mg or more of ascorbic acid (vitamin C). Avoid tea containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, and milk and dairy products, during the period of use and just before and after a dose.

If hives, itching, a hypersensitivity reaction of the skin on exposure to sunlight, abdominal or stomach pain, stomach cramps, vomiting, diarrhoea, fever or coma occurs, or from time to time a rise in AST and ALT, or rarely a rise in ALP, nausea, loss of appetite, constipation, black stools, discoloration of the teeth or stomach discomfort, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Lotion (340100CLT)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for pain relief and the reduction of inflammation in sprains, bruises, muscle pain, joint pain, fracture pain, back pain, stiff shoulders, neuralgia, rheumatic pain, itching of the skin, insect bites and chilblains.

Be careful that it does not get into the eyes, and if it does, wash it out with water at once.
Do not wrap or bandage the treated area, and do not expose it to outside heat or hot water.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 or 6 days of use, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

If rash or reddening or itching occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Syrup (B89400ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat (pain in the throat), cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 30 mL at a time. Those aged 11 years and over but under 15 years: take 20 mL at a time. Those aged 7 years and over but under 11 years: take 15 mL at a time. Those aged 3 years and over but under 7 years: take 10 mL at a time. Those aged 2 years and over but under 3 years: take 7.5 mL at a time. Take it after every meal and, if needed, at bedtime. As a rule, leave an interval of 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage. Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported; if a skin rash or another sign of hypersensitivity appears after a dose of this medicine, stop taking it at once. Do not go above the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had it, if you have had asthma when taking another antipyretic analgesic or cold medicine, if the user is an infant under 3 months of age, or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the last 2 weeks. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is an infant aged 3 months and over but under 2 years; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you are an older person or physically weak; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you have a high fever, heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain or another stomach problem, an ulcer or a bleeding problem; or if you smoke, or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with a lot of phlegm, a cough lasting or coming back for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or a persistent headache. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after a dose, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, anti-Parkinson medicines and the like), cough and expectorant medicines, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, travel sickness medicines, allergy medicines). Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.

If rash, reddening, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema (swelling), difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, shock (hives, swelling and tightness of the chest immediately after a dose, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms with high fever, and a rash or reddening with burn-like blisters, on the skin of the whole body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, asthma, generalised weakness, jaundice or interstitial pneumonia (cough with shortness of breath, difficulty breathing and fever) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (A14400ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for contraception.
groups.usage: Take 1 tablet in 1 day for 21 days in the order marked on the pack, and then have 7 days without tablets. It is best to take it at the same time every day where possible. Menstruation occurs during the 7 tablet-free days and usually starts within 2 to 3 days after the last tablet. If you go on with this medicine, start the tablets from a new pack after the 7 tablet-free days; menstruation may not have finished before the new pack is started. For details such as what to do if a dose is missed or if the cycle is to be changed, refer to the detailed approved product information.
groups.caution:
The risk of serious cardiovascular events such as thrombosis may be increased, so women taking an oral contraceptive should not smoke. Smokers aged 35 years and over must not take this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had an oestrogen-dependent tumour (for example breast cancer, cancer of the lining of the womb); if you have or have had thrombotic arteritis or phlebitis or thromboembolism, deep vein thrombosis, or an inherited or acquired tendency to thrombosis; if you have cerebrovascular or coronary artery disease (in particular myocardial infarction); if you are at high risk of venous or arterial thrombosis; if you have abnormal genital bleeding that has not been diagnosed; if you have moderate or severe high blood pressure, moderate or severe liver disorder, Dubin-Johnson syndrome or Rotor syndrome, jaundice, cholestasis, hepatitis or a benign or malignant liver tumour; if you have sickle cell anaemia; if you have a severe metabolic disorder such as severe diabetes with damage to the blood vessels, severe hyperlipidaemia, hyperlipoproteinaemia or porphyria; if you have had persistent itching in pregnancy, herpes gestationis, pemphigoid gestationis or otosclerosis; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have a pituitary tumour or a high prolactin level that may be accompanied by discharge of milk; if you have migraine with warning symptoms such as scintillating scotoma or fortification spectra; if you have valvular heart disease with pulmonary hypertension or atrial fibrillation; if you have had subacute bacterial endocarditis; if you have valvular heart disease; if you have diabetes with damage to the blood vessels (diabetic kidney disease, diabetic retinopathy and the like); if you have a history of pancreatitis or of severe hypertriglyceridaemia; if you have headache with focal neurological symptoms such as an aura; if you are receiving a direct-acting antiviral medicine for hepatitis C; if you are a smoker aged 35 years and over; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are a woman aged 40 years and over; if you have epilepsy; if you have had breast cancer; if you have or have had depression; if you have heart or kidney failure; if you have atypical hyperplastic breast disease; if you have had a breast lump; if you have had hyperlipidaemia; if you have had gallbladder disease or gallstones; if you have endometriosis, asthma or melasma; if you have a disorder of the peripheral circulation; or if you have severe gastrointestinal disorder.
This medicine does not protect against HIV infection (AIDS) or other sexually transmitted infections.
This medicine is not for use in girls before their first period or in women after the menopause.

groups.title: Syrup (185430ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for allergic rhinitis (sneezing, blocked nose, itching, a burning feeling in the eyes) and for chronic idiopathic urticaria (hives of unknown cause).
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and over: take 10 mL, 1 time in 1 day. Children aged 2 years and over but under 12 years: if the body weight is 30 kg or more, take 10 mL, 1 time in 1 day; if the body weight is 30 kg or less, take 5 mL, 1 time in 1 day. The dose may be increased or decreased as appropriate according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a child under 2 years of age, or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have liver disorder or kidney failure.

Do not take it together with cimetidine, erythromycin, ketoconazole, quinidine, fluconazole or fluoxetine.

If sedation, an anticholinergic effect, headache, fainting, drowsiness, thirst, gastrointestinal disturbance (nausea, gastritis), increased appetite, rapid heartbeat, tiredness, rash, hair loss, anaphylaxis including angioedema, liver dysfunction, supraventricular tachyarrhythmia, palpitations, dizziness or seizures occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Syrup (A18300ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to prevent and relieve the dizziness, vomiting and headache of travel sickness.
groups.usage: Those aged 15 years and over: take 1 sachet (6 mL) at a time. Those aged 13 years and over but under 15 years: take 2/3 sachet (4 mL) at a time. The number of doses in 1 day is limited to 3. To prevent travel sickness, take it 30 minutes before boarding the vehicle or boat. If a further dose is needed, leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
This medicine contains aspartame, which is broken down in the body to phenylalanine, so people with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their intake of phenylalanine must not take it.

Infants and young children under 3 years of age, and children aged 12 years and under, must not take this medicine. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have had symptoms of hypersensitivity to this medicine (rash, reddening, itching and the like); if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you have a respiratory disease such as emphysema or chronic bronchitis; or if you are an older person. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after a dose, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with other anti-sickness medicines, cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, antihistamines, sedatives or cough and expectorant medicines. Avoid alcoholic drinks while you are taking it.

If rash, reddening, itching or thirst occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
