groups.title: Tablet (D99400ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills (feeling cold and shivering), fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults: take 2 tablets at a time, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.
Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported; if a skin rash or another sign of hypersensitivity appears after a dose of this medicine, stop taking it at once.
Do not go above the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had it; if you have had asthma when taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is an infant under 3 months of age; if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure, or severe acute or chronic kidney disease or kidney failure.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) appear in connection with the pseudoephedrine component; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain, blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain or another stomach problem that lasts or comes back, or an ulcer or a bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke, or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with a lot of phlegm, a cough lasting or coming back for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or a persistent headache.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 or 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
Drowsiness may occur after a dose, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with cough and expectorant medicines, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, travel sickness medicines, allergy medicines).
Do not take this medicine if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the last 2 weeks.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, preparations containing potassium, preparations containing liquorice, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid), thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide) or flucloxacillin.
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.

If rash or reddening, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia or high anion gap metabolic acidosis occurs, or rarely shock (hives, swelling and tightness of the chest immediately after a dose, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms with high fever, and a rash or reddening with burn-like blisters), asthma, generalised weakness, jaundice, interstitial pneumonia (cough with shortness of breath, difficulty breathing and fever), a fall in the amount of urine with swelling of the face, hands and feet, heavy eyelids, stiff hands, a rise in blood pressure, headache, muscle disease (weakness, cramps of the limbs, paralysis), or symptoms of reversible posterior encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (a sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance), stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft capsule (E19000ACS)

If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had it, if you have had asthma when taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine, if the user is an infant under 3 months of age, or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the last 2 weeks.

groups.title: Cream (A39600CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the symptoms of varicose veins (pain, a heavy feeling, swelling of the legs, cramp in the calf muscles), for blunt injury from an accident or from sport (haematoma, bruising, contusion, strain, sprain, swelling, pain of muscles and ligaments), and for superficial phlebitis, thrombophlebitis and treatment after sclerotherapy.
groups.usage: Use about 5 cm of the cream, apply it to the affected area and to the skin around it 2 to 3 times every day, and rub in gently. When applying it to the leg, massage lightly from below upwards. For phlebitis, do not rub it in; spread it thinly and then cover it with an occlusive dressing. This medicine has a strong cooling effect, so it is suitable for sensitive areas and for large areas.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to heparin, if you have a tendency to bleed or a low platelet count, or if you have thrombosis or thromboembolism; and do not use it on open wounds, on mucous membranes or on areas with a pus-forming infection. Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding. Avoid contact with the conjunctiva of the eye.

If an allergy rarely occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Ointment (339200COM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to prevent infection in minor cuts, grazes and burns.
groups.usage: After cleaning the wound, apply an appropriate amount to the wound 1 to 3 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or a perforated eardrum, and do not use it around the eyes. Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have a severe wound, a severe burn, a puncture wound, an animal bite or an ulcer of the skin. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is used for a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. This medicine is for external use only; it must not be swallowed.

If rash, itching, reddening, swelling, papules, small blisters, a feeling of irritation or a superimposed infection occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of headache, toothache, pain after a tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia, back pain, muscle pain, stiff shoulders, bruising pain, fracture pain, sprain pain, menstrual pain (period pain) and pain from injury, and to bring down fever when there are chills and a raised temperature.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet at a time, up to 3 times in 1 day, avoiding an empty stomach and leaving an interval of at least 4 hours between doses. As a rule this medicine is for short-term use, and children under 15 years of age must not take it.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.
Do not go above the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you have had asthma when taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine, if you have glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency, acute intermittent porphyria, granulocytopenia, severe liver disorder or kidney disorder, a tendency to bleed or a peptic ulcer, if the user is a child under 15 years of age, or if you have a severe blood disorder or severely reduced heart function.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching); if the user is an adolescent aged 15 years and over who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have thyroid disease, diabetes or high blood pressure; if you are physically weak, have a high fever or are an older person; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain or another stomach problem that lasts or comes back; if you have liver disorder or have had it, kidney disorder or have had it, peptic ulcer or have had it, a blood disorder or have had one, a tendency to bleed, abnormal heart function, hypersensitivity or a history of it, or bronchial asthma; or if you have been taking warfarin over a long period.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 or 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Without the advice of a doctor or pharmacist, do not take it for pain for 10 days or more or for fever for 3 days or more.

Do not take it together with other anti-inflammatory analgesics, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with lithium or thiazide diuretics.

If shock symptoms (difficulty breathing, reddening of the whole body, swelling of the blood vessels, hives, an asthma attack, or swelling and tightness of the chest immediately after a dose together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and shortness of breath), a fall in platelets, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia (destruction of red cells), methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, facial swelling, difficulty breathing, sweating, low blood pressure, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, rash, an allergic reaction, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome — severe symptoms such as high fever, rash, reddening and burn-like blisters on the skin of the whole body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth and eyes), generalised weakness, jaundice, cough with shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever, or high anion gap metabolic acidosis occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area 1 to several times in 1 day. The amount may be increased or decreased as appropriate according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had it; if you have a tuberculous, viral or other pus-forming infection of the mouth; or if you have syphilis, chickenpox, a fungal infection, a bacterial skin infection, dermatitis around the mouth, rosacea, or gingivitis due to lack of vitamin C.
Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant, if the user is an infant or a child, or if the user is an older person.
Do not eat food immediately after use.
Do not use this medicine for the eyes.

If an infection of the mouth (a fungal or bacterial infection of the mouth) occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
A feeling of numbness in the mouth, an abnormal or reduced sense of taste and, rarely, an allergic reaction may occur.

groups.caution:

When it is taken with other medicines, leave an interval of 2 hours between them.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have liver disorder or heart disorder, if you have had gastric or duodenal ulcer, if you are pregnant or breast-feeding, if you are an older person, or if you have hypersensitivity to caramel or have had it.

Do not mix it with syrups containing antibiotics or trimetoquinol hydrochloride; take them separately.

If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills (feeling cold and shivering), fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet at a time, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.
Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported; if a skin rash or another sign of hypersensitivity appears after a dose of this medicine, stop taking it at once.
Do not go above the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had it, if the user is an infant under 3 months of age, if you have had asthma when taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine, if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the last 2 weeks, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is an infant or young child aged 3 months and over but under 2 years; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you are an older person or physically weak; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer or a high fever; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain or another stomach problem that lasts or comes back, or an ulcer or a bleeding problem; or if you have hypersensitivity to Food Yellow No. 4 or have had it.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
Drowsiness may occur after a dose, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 or 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, anti-Parkinson medicines and the like), cough and expectorant medicines, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, travel sickness medicines, allergy medicines).
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol.
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.

If rash, reddening, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, shock (hives, swelling and tightness of the chest immediately after a dose, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms with high fever, and a rash or reddening with burn-like blisters, on the skin of the whole body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, generalised weakness, jaundice or interstitial pneumonia (cough with shortness of breath, difficulty breathing and fever) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Oral liquid (533700ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for iron deficiency anaemia.
groups.usage: Take 1 bottle at a time, 2 times in 1 day. Press down firmly on the raised part of the upper cap, shake well so that the powder and the liquid mix thoroughly, then turn the upper cap to the left to open it and take the contents.
groups.caution:
An overdose in a child aged 6 years or under can cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep it out of the reach of children.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is an infant under 12 months of age; or if you have haemochromatosis (a disease in which iron is deposited in the liver and pancreas because of abnormal iron metabolism), haemosiderosis, anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency, aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia (destruction of red cells), anaemia in which iron cannot be used, or chronic pancreatitis.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional colitis, impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney disorder, or a low protein level in the blood.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics or antacids.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with anti-aldosterone medicines, triamterene, quinolones, penicillamine, chloramphenicol, cholestyramine, pancreatic extract, preparations such as vitamin E, or 200 mg or more of ascorbic acid (vitamin C).
Avoid tea containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, and milk and dairy products, during the period of use and just before and after a dose.

If hives, itching, a hypersensitivity reaction of the skin on exposure to sunlight, abdominal or stomach pain, stomach cramps, stomach discomfort, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation, loss of appetite, fever or coma occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Lotion (A44200CLT)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the disinfection of the hands of surgeons and of health and hygiene workers at the time of surgery.
groups.usage:
For surgical hand disinfection: every day before use, clean under the nails with a nail stick, then apply the product to clean, dry hands and nails. Pump 2 mL of the product into the palm of one hand and, with the fingers of the other hand, work it under the nails. Spread the rest evenly over the hand and up to the elbow, then pump a further 2 mL and repeat the same steps on the other hand. Pump 2 mL once more, apply it over both hands and up to the wrists, and let it dry before putting gloves on.
For hand disinfection by health and hygiene workers: apply it to clean, dry hands and nails. Pump 2 mL of the product into the palm of one hand. Then spread it evenly over both hands and up to the wrists, paying particular attention to the spaces between the fingers and under the nails, and let it dry without wiping it off.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if there is a wound deeper than a break in the outer layer of the skin, or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist before using it if you have or have had an allergic disease such as asthma, or if it is to be used on broken skin (especially a burn).
Do not swallow it or inject it; it must be used externally only.
It must not come into contact with the brain, the meninges, the eyes, the ears, the mouth or mucous membranes (especially the mucous membranes of the genitals), and if there is a perforated eardrum keep it away from the ear canal.
Never touch the eyes with hands on which this medicine has been used.
Contact with the eye can cause serious damage to the cornea that may require a corneal graft (corneal erosion, loss of the surface layer or damage to the cornea, and serious permanent loss of sight), so be careful that it does not get into the eyes; if it does, wash them out at once and thoroughly with clean water.
It is a flammable liquid and there is a risk of burns, so let it dry before using electrical equipment.
Do not mix it with other chemicals or with cleaning agents.
Do not use it to disinfect surgical instruments.

Its action may be blocked (inactivated), so avoid using this medicine and soap at the same time or one straight after the other.
Do not combine it with anionic derivatives.

If irritation, sensitisation, an allergic reaction or, rarely, anaphylactic shock occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.usage: Adults: as a starting dose take 140 mg at a time (or 60 mg at a time as silibinin), 3 times in 1 day; as a maintenance dose take 70 mg at a time (or 30 mg at a time as silibinin), 3 times in 1 day, or 140 mg at a time (or 60 mg as silibinin), 2 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you have severe obstruction of the bile duct, or if the user is a child aged 12 years or under. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant or breast-feeding, or if you have jaundice. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

If stomach pain, diarrhoea or an allergic reaction rarely occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (D69100ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins B1, B2, B6 and C in physical tiredness, in pregnancy and breast-feeding and when strength is reduced during or after an illness; for the relief of neuralgia, muscle pain and joint pain (back pain, stiff shoulders and the like); for beriberi and tired eyes; for the relief of angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis; and to supply zinc.
groups.usage: Those aged 8 years and over and adults: take 1 tablet at a time, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a baby under 12 months of age, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or an infant; if you have high oxalate levels in the urine; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney disorder, a low protein level in the blood, gout or kidney stones; or if you are short of folic acid. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. It can interfere with the detection of sugar in urine tests and can turn the urine yellow, so it may affect laboratory test results.

Do not take it together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with anti-aldosterone medicines or triamterene. Avoid tea containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, during the period of use and just before and after a dose.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, loose stools, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure or fluid in the lungs occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Ointment (D04800COM)

groups.usage: Adults aged 15 years and over: apply an appropriate amount directly to the affected area 1 to 3 times in 1 day. Children under 15 years of age: apply an appropriate amount directly to the affected area 1 to 3 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if the affected area has become filled with pus, if you have heart disease, high blood pressure, thyroid disease or diabetes, if you have difficulty passing urine because of an enlarged prostate, or if you are breast-feeding. Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is used for a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Use this medicine only in the anus, and do not use it for the eyes.

Do not use it together with suppositories, ointments or creams containing dl-methylephedrine hydrochloride, scopolia extract or glycyrrhizic acid, or with medicines that lower blood pressure or with antidepressants.

If swelling, a feeling of irritation, allergic symptoms (rash, reddening, itching and the like), bleeding or blurred vision (frequency unknown) occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft capsule (E92700ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins A, D, E, B1, B2, B6 and C in physical tiredness, in pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after an illness, during growth and in later life; for the relief of dryness of the eyes and for night blindness; for poor growth of the bones and teeth and the prevention of rickets; for the prevention and treatment of iron deficiency anaemia; and to supply zinc.
groups.usage: Those aged 12 years and over and adults: take 1 capsule at a time, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If a pregnant woman takes 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A in 1 day it can cause birth defects. Women in the first 3 months of pregnancy, or who may be pregnant, must not take it.
Keep it out of the reach of children. Iron-containing preparations can cause fatal poisoning if a child aged 6 years or under accidentally takes too much.

Do not take this medicine if you have a high calcium level in the blood, sarcoidosis (a generalised inflammatory disease of unknown cause) or kidney disease; if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have a high potassium level in the blood, haemochromatosis (a disease in which iron is deposited in the liver and pancreas because of abnormal iron metabolism), haemosiderosis, anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency, kidney stones or severe kidney failure; or if you have hypersensitivity to soya-bean oil or have had an allergic reaction to it, or hypersensitivity to soya or peanut.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have high oxalate levels in the urine; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or an infant; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional colitis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney disorder or a low protein level in the blood; if you have gallbladder disease, liver disease, acute or chronic bronchitis, fluid in the lungs, alkalosis, peptic ulcer, diabetes, or gout or kidney stones, or have had kidney stones; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or fat emulsions must be given to you with care; if you have hypersensitivity to Food Yellow No. 5 or Sunset Yellow FCF or have had an allergic reaction to them; or if fat overload is a concern for you.
If you have a tendency to thrombosis, or if you are short of folic acid, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
The vitamin A in this medicine is supplied in sufficient amounts by a normal diet, so as a supplement do not go above 5,000 IU in 1 day.
It can interfere with the detection of sugar in urine tests and can turn the urine yellow, so it may affect laboratory test results.

Do not take it together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen, anti-aldosterone medicines, triamterene or intravenous lipid preparations.
Avoid tea containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, during the period of use and just before and after a dose.

If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry and rough skin, painful swelling of the joints, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, reddening, loose stools, hives, a photosensitivity reaction, abdominal or stomach pain, cramps, fever, coma, an allergic reaction, angioedema, joint pain, a rise in eosinophils, iodine poisoning, a high potassium level, wind, stomach pain, dermatitis, an unpleasant smell of sweat or breath, hair loss, impatience, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure or fluid in the lungs occurs, or if a period comes earlier than expected, the bleeding gradually becomes heavier, or bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft capsule (E30600ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of headache, toothache, pain after a tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia, back pain, muscle pain, stiff shoulders, bruising pain, fracture pain, sprain pain, menstrual pain (period pain) and pain from injury, and to bring down fever when there are chills (feeling cold and shivering) and a raised temperature.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 1 capsule at a time, 1 to 3 times in 1 day, avoiding an empty stomach. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease should use ibuprofen only after careful consideration and should avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg in 1 day). People with cardiovascular risk factors (for example high blood pressure, high blood fats, diabetes, smoking) who need high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg in 1 day) should consider carefully before starting long-term treatment. Clinical studies have shown that high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg in 1 day) may slightly increase the risk of arterial thrombotic events (myocardial infarction or stroke).

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you have had asthma with this medicine or with another antipyretic analgesic or cold medicine, or if the user is an infant under 3 months of age.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, thyroid disease, diabetes or high blood pressure; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you are an older person; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain or another stomach problem that lasts or comes back, or an ulcer or a bleeding problem; if you have lost a lot of body fluid through vomiting and diarrhoea or are unable to take fluid in; if you have hypersensitivity to Food Yellow No. 5 or have had it; or if the user is a child under 2 years of age.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 or 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take it together with other antipyretic analgesics, cold medicines or sedatives.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, diuretics or low-dose aspirin.
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.

If rash or reddening, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, stomach pain, bleeding from the digestive tract, stomach discomfort, dizziness or oedema occurs, or rarely shock (hives, swelling and tightness of the chest immediately after a dose, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome — severe symptoms with high fever, and a rash or reddening with burn-like blisters, on the skin of the whole body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, or very rarely erythema multiforme, exfoliative dermatitis, a photosensitivity reaction of unknown frequency, drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) or acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Headache, toothache and pain after tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint, nerve, back and muscle pain, stiff shoulders, injury pain and period pain, and fever

groups.title: Capsule (433200ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills (feeling cold and shivering), fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Those aged 8 years and over but under 11 years: take 1 capsule at a time. Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 2 capsules at a time. Take it 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.
Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported; if a skin rash or another sign of hypersensitivity appears after a dose of this medicine, stop taking it at once.
Do not go above the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had it, if you have had asthma when taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine, if the user is a child under 2 years of age, if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure, or if you have severe acute or chronic kidney disease or kidney failure.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) appear in connection with the pseudoephedrine component; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, oedema, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain, blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain or another stomach problem that lasts or comes back, or an ulcer or a bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke, or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with a lot of phlegm, a cough lasting or coming back for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or a persistent headache.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 or 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
Drowsiness may occur after a dose, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with cough and expectorant medicines, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, travel sickness medicines, allergy medicines).
Do not take this medicine if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the last 2 weeks.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, preparations containing potassium, preparations containing liquorice, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid), thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide) or flucloxacillin.
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.

If rash or reddening, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia or high anion gap metabolic acidosis occurs, or rarely shock (hives, swelling and tightness of the chest immediately after a dose, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms with high fever, and a rash or reddening with burn-like blisters), acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, a severe skin reaction such as fever, erythema and many small pustules, asthma, generalised weakness, jaundice, interstitial pneumonia (cough with shortness of breath, difficulty breathing and fever), a fall in the amount of urine with swelling of the face, hands and feet, heavy eyelids, stiff hands, a rise in blood pressure or headache, muscle disease (weakness, cramps of the limbs, paralysis), or symptoms of reversible posterior encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (a sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance), stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (110401ATB)

groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, high oxalate levels in the urine, thalassaemia, gout, cystinuria, glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency, or oxalate kidney stones (when 1 g or more is taken in 1 day).

When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

It can interfere with the detection of sugar in urine tests.

Avoid drinking or smoking to excess.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with oral anticoagulants (coumarin medicines), salicylates, aspirin, iron preparations, phenytoin and some antiepileptic medicines, oral contraceptives containing oestrogen, tetracycline antibiotics, fluphenazine, orlistat, barbiturate derivatives or corticosteroids.

If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

People with cardiovascular risk factors (for example high blood pressure, high blood fats, diabetes, smoking) who need high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg in 1 day) should consider carefully before starting long-term treatment. Clinical studies have shown that high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg in 1 day) may slightly increase the risk of arterial thrombotic events (myocardial infarction or stroke).

groups.usage: Those aged 15 years and over: take 2 tablets at a time, 3 times in 1 day, avoiding an empty stomach, leaving an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal effects such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had asthma, hives or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic (including COX-2 inhibitors); if you have peptic ulcer or a severe blood disorder; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; for pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG); or if the user is a child under 15 years of age.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have had peptic ulcer, if you have liver disorder now or in the past, kidney disorder now or in the past, or heart failure; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you are an older person; or if you take low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 or 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take it together with other antipyretic analgesics, cold medicines, sedatives or travel sickness medicines.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, digoxin, phenytoin, baclofen, diuretics, antihypertensive medicines, ACE inhibitors, furosemide, aspirin, lithium, methotrexate or oral anticoagulants (such as warfarin).

If nausea, a feeling of abdominal bloating, stomach pain, heartburn, loss of appetite, diarrhoea, constipation, vomiting, gastritis or excessive hidden bleeding occurs, or rarely ulceration of the digestive tract with bleeding, or from time to time effects on the central nervous system, headache, depression, dizziness, insomnia, fear, disturbed consciousness, tinnitus, hearing loss or weak sight, or rarely hives, purpura, itching or rash, or very rarely Stevens-Johnson syndrome, a photosensitivity reaction (frequency unknown), erythema multiforme, exfoliative dermatitis, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome, frequency unknown) or acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, or rarely jaundice or a rise in GOT, GPT or ALP, or rarely aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, autoimmune haemorrhagic anaemia, bleeding, granulocytopenia, a fall in platelets or reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), or rarely acute kidney failure, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine or a rise in BUN or blood creatinine, a high potassium level in the blood, generalised oedema or Kounis syndrome, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft capsule (E83800ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins A, E, B1 and B2 in physical tiredness, in pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after an illness and in later life; for the relief of dryness of the eyes and for night blindness; for neuralgia, muscle pain and joint pain (back pain, stiff shoulders and the like); for beriberi and tired eyes; for the relief of angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis; and to supply zinc.
groups.usage: Those aged 12 years and over and adults: take 2 capsules at a time, 2 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Taking 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A in 1 day can cause birth defects. Women in the first 3 months of pregnancy, or who may be pregnant, must not take it.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a baby under 12 months of age, or if you have hypersensitivity to soya-bean oil, soya or peanut or have had an allergic reaction to them.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or an infant; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney disorder or a low protein level in the blood; or if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or fat emulsions must be given to you with care.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
It can interfere with the detection of sugar in urine tests and can turn the urine yellow, so it may affect laboratory test results.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take it together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations or antacids.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with anti-aldosterone medicines or triamterene.
Avoid tea containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, during the period of use and just before and after a dose.

If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry and rough skin, painful swelling of the joints, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, rash, reddening, loose stools, loss of appetite, erythema (red patches), hives, eczema, a maculopapular rash, oedema, or oedema and fluid retention (in people with kidney failure or heart failure), gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure or fluid in the lungs occurs, or if a period comes earlier than expected, the bleeding gradually becomes heavier, or bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Ointment (B34800COM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the temporary relief of the pain, itching, swelling and bleeding of anal fissure and haemorrhoids.
groups.usage: Apply an appropriate amount directly to the affected area, or introduce it into the rectum, 1 to 3 times in 1 day. For use in the rectum, fit the applicator to the tube and insert it into the rectum.
groups.caution:
People whose affected area has become filled with pus, people with heart disease, high blood pressure, thyroid disease or diabetes, people with difficulty passing urine because of an enlarged prostate, women who are breast-feeding, and children must not use this medicine. Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Use this medicine only around the anus, and do not use it for the eyes. If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 week of use, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not use it together with suppositories, ointments or creams containing dl-methylephedrine hydrochloride, scopolia extract or glycyrrhizic acid, or with medicines that lower blood pressure or with antidepressants.

If reddening, swelling, a feeling of irritation, the formation of pus, allergic symptoms (rash, reddening, itching and the like), bleeding or blurred vision (frequency unknown) occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (C35300ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for diarrhoea, diarrhoea with abdominal pain, a feeling of food not going down, loose stools, and vomiting with diarrhoea.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 1 capsule at a time, 3 times in 1 day. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
Women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, women who are breast-feeding, newborn babies, children aged 7 years and under, and people with a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption, must not take this medicine. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (rash, reddening, itching and the like), if you are an older person, or if you have diarrhoea with fever, blood or mucus in the stool, or gastric or duodenal ulcer. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not keep taking it for 3 days or more.

Do not take it together with gastrointestinal analgesic and antispasmodic medicines. Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.

If rash, itching or, rarely, dry mouth occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.usage: Those aged 8 years and over and adults: take 1 tablet at a time, 1 time in 1 day, after a meal.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or an infant; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney disorder or a low protein level in the blood; or if you are short of folic acid.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
It can turn the urine yellow and so affect laboratory test results.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take it together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa.
Do not take it together with anti-aldosterone medicines or triamterene.
Avoid tea containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, during the period of use and just before and after a dose.

groups.title: Cream (D67000CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for pain relief and the reduction of inflammation in sprains, bruises and muscle pain.
groups.usage: Apply a thin layer of about 1 to 4 cm to the affected area 3 times in 1 day and rub in gently so that it is absorbed well. Without the advice of a doctor, the treatment period should not go beyond 5 days.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had hypersensitivity to aspirin or a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic (an asthma attack, hives, rhinitis); if the user is a child aged 12 years or under; if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; or if you have gastric or duodenal ulcer.
Do not use it in or around the eyes, on mucous membranes, on eczema, on dermatitis caused by lacquer and the like, on wounds or inflamed areas, on sensitive skin, on a bleeding skin condition, on infected skin, or on burns.
Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have bronchial asthma, kidney disease or an allergic constitution, if the skin is very moist or badly broken down, if you have a circulatory disorder or diabetes, or if you have hypersensitivity to propylene glycol or have had it.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
This medicine is for external use only; it must not be swallowed.
Be careful that it does not get into the eyes, and if it does, wash it out at once with water.
Do not cover it with an airtight dressing.
When it is used for a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you use it together with medicines that lower blood pressure.

If rash or reddening, itching, flushing, stinging pain, a skin rash, peeling of the skin, dry skin, an abscess, the formation of pustules, hives, a burning sensation, a skin reaction, bronchospasm, a fall in blood pressure leading to shock, or aseptic meningitis (headache, nausea, vomiting, fever, a stiff neck or clouding of consciousness) occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
If erythema multiforme, exfoliative dermatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) very rarely occurs, or drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) or acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis of unknown frequency, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft capsule (E85800ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of blocked nose, runny nose, sneezing, watering eyes, sore throat and a heavy feeling in the head caused by a nasal cold (acute rhinitis), allergic rhinitis or sinusitis.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 1 capsule at a time, 3 times in 1 day, after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a child under 2 years of age, or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the last 2 weeks.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to Food Yellow No. 4 (tartrazine); if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have heart disease, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you are an older person; or if you smoke, or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with a lot of phlegm, a cough lasting or coming back for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or a persistent headache.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
Do not keep taking it over a long period.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 or 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Drowsiness may occur after a dose of this medicine, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with other oral medicines for rhinitis or with oral medicines containing antihistamines (cold medicines, cough and expectorant medicines, travel sickness medicines, allergy medicines and the like).
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.

If haemorrhagic stroke, nausea or vomiting, persistent or severe thirst, constipation, loss of appetite, rash or reddening, itching, difficulty passing urine, headache, facial flushing or unusual sensitivity to light occurs, or rarely shock (anaphylaxis — hives, swelling and tightness of the chest immediately after a dose, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft capsule (E65100ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat (pain in the throat), cough, phlegm, chills (feeling cold and shivering), fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 2 capsules at a time, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.
Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported; if a skin rash or another sign of hypersensitivity appears after a dose of this medicine, stop taking it at once.
Do not go above the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is an infant under 3 months of age or a child under 2 years of age; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the last 2 weeks; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) appear in connection with the pseudoephedrine component; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain, blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain or another stomach problem that lasts or comes back, or an ulcer or a bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke, or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with a lot of phlegm, a cough lasting or coming back for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or a persistent headache.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 or 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
Drowsiness may occur after a dose, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with cough and expectorant medicines, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, travel sickness medicines, allergy medicines).
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol.
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.

If rash or reddening, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, or rarely shock (hives, swelling and tightness of the chest, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome — severe symptoms with high fever, and a rash or reddening with burn-like blisters, on the skin of the whole body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, liver dysfunction (generalised weakness, jaundice — yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes), interstitial pneumonia (cough with shortness of breath, difficulty breathing and fever), or a sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures or visual disturbance, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
